title: Bearing Lite System One deterministic-execution backends (jev, laya, validator)
description: One schema family ("system1") for three distinct verification backend identities: the decision models `jev` and `laya`, and `validator`, a pinned deterministic program (no model, no probability) for rules expressible as code. A System One decision model scores fixed, typed options for a fixed input; it never generates text. Bearing uses it only for deterministic execution: a frozen, versioned rubric pins exactly one backend, one immutable model revision, one typed question, fixed thresholds, a replay protocol, and a gateway cache policy, so a verdict is mechanically derived and reproducible. Three document shapes: (a) `rubric` - the frozen rubric definition, discriminated on `backend`; (b) `command_configuration` - the object hooks/verification-bridge.cjs planVerification stores in a request and receipt for this backend; (c) `backend_output` - the run output handed to sealVerification, whose SHA-256 over canonical JSON becomes the receipt `evidence_digest`. Schema validates structure only; hooks/verification.cjs still enforces diagnostic-versus-assurance authority, independence, and gate eligibility. No valid document carries a credential, key, or account id: secrets are referenced only by environment-variable name.

git_sha.description: Immutable Hugging Face commit sha (40 hex). A branch or tag name such as `main` is mutable and invalid.

semver.description: Exact version. Ranges, `latest`, and prerelease tags are invalid because they are not reproducible.

env_var_name.description: Name of an environment variable that holds a secret or deployment-specific value. Only the NAME is recorded; the value never appears in a rubric, request, receipt, or output.

backend.description: Distinct backend identity. `jev`, `laya` and `validator` share the system1 schema family but are never interchangeable: switching backend is a different binding and a different receipt, and requires a plan amendment. A generic name such as `system1` must not stand in for any of them. `validator` is a program, not the retired Validator role.

verdict_operation.description: Verdict-only backend operations. Each scores the rubric's fixed options for the fixed input and returns an answer plus probability; none proposes, generates, or rewrites a claim or an option.

generative_operation.description: Operations that would propose, generate, or rewrite claims, options, or code, or perform open-ended judgment. Listed in `denied` so planVerification refuses them as `generative_backend_operation_denied` rather than `backend_operation_unsupported`.

backend_operations.description: Operation policy copied verbatim into the planVerification spec `backend_operations`. `allowed` is verdict-only; `denied` must name at least the core generative operations.

laya_checkpoint.description: `laya` = ModernBERT-large, 421M, 512-token context (English). `laya-multilingual` = mmBERT-base, 322M, 1024-token default context (encoder reads up to 8192 with max_len). `laya-typed-decisions` = ModernBERT-large fine-tune, 421M, 1024-token context. All three live in the `convaiinnovations/laya` repository (root and subfolders).

question_type.description: `choice` = one of named options; `score` = ordinal level from an ordered list; `noul` = binary yes/no (the backend returns the probability of yes).

laya_model.description: Open-weights Laya pin. Weights are fetched only by immutable commit; a Router may be used only when `selection` allows it.

selection.description: `pinned` calls the named checkpoint directly (Router `model=` override or single-model load). `router_auto` lets the Laya Router choose by detected language/script; because that choice depends on the input, it is diagnostic-only and invalid on an assurance-eligible rubric. When the served routing metadata names a checkpoint other than `checkpoint`, the run is ERROR `checkpoint_mismatch`.

eval_mode.description: Model runs in eval mode (dropout off). Training-mode inference is never valid.

fast_path.description: Whether the optional TileLang GPU fast path is enabled. Recorded because it changes kernels and therefore bit-level results; replay epsilon absorbs residual GPU nondeterminism only.

max_len.description: Total sequence budget passed to the runtime. Must not exceed the checkpoint limit (512 for `laya`, 1024 for `laya-typed-decisions`, 8192 for `laya-multilingual`).

head_max_len.description: Option-prompt budget. State budget is max_len - head_max_len.

jev_model.description: Hosted TypeSafe Jev pin. The model version is the immutable revision; a response reporting any other version is ERROR `model_revision_mismatch`.

function.description: Vercel AI SDK evaluation entry point. Text-generation entry points are never used.

question.description: The single typed question, exactly as sent in the `/v1/systemone` `questions` map (Jev and laya-serve share this shape). `question_digest` in the rubric is SHA-256 over canonical JSON of this object.

criteria.description: `choice`: object mapping option key to a description. `score`: ordered array of level descriptions (index = level). `noul`: absent.

decision.description: Frozen mapping from (hard answer, calibrated probability) to status. Per run: VERIFIED iff the hard answer is in `claim_holds_options` AND the calibrated probability mass of `claim_holds_options` >= `verify_threshold`; REFUTED iff the hard answer is in `claim_fails_options` AND the mass of `claim_fails_options` >= `refute_threshold`; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE. The two option sets are disjoint; an option in neither set (for example an explicit `unclear`) always maps to INCONCLUSIVE. Thresholds are frozen in the plan and never chosen at run time.

claim_holds_options.description: Option keys (choice), level indexes as decimal strings (score), or `yes`/`no` (noul) whose selection means the claim holds.

probability_basis.description: Thresholds compare against the calibrated probability summed over the relevant option set, never the raw logit, the `act_probability` head, or an uncalibrated softmax.

tie_rule.description: An exact tie for the top option (or noul p(yes) == 0.5) is INCONCLUSIVE `answer_tie`; there is no lexical or first-listed tie-break.

calibration.description: How the probability compared against the thresholds was calibrated, and on what frozen data. Recalibrating changes the rubric version.

method.description: `temperature_scaled`: one frozen temperature per (question type, option count), fitted on the named calibration set. `provider_as_returned`: probabilities used as the hosted provider returns them (Jev only).

max_ece.description: Ceiling on measured ECE for this rubric's calibration set. A rubric whose measured_ece exceeds it must not be frozen.

input_policy.description: What the model sees and how it is made byte-stable. The canonicalized input is SHA-256 digested; that digest is bound into the claim and the evidence.

state_shape.description: `text` = a single string state; `json_document` = a JSON object state; `keyed_text` = an object of named text fields (for example {"document": ...}).

locator.description: Repository-relative path, glob, or extractor id resolved against the candidate. Never an absolute host path or URL carrying credentials.

extractor.description: Deterministic extraction step (for example a JSON pointer or a named parser) applied before canonicalization.

canonicalization.description: Byte-stable normalization applied before digesting and sending. The exact bytes sent are the bytes digested.

token_limit.description: Maximum state tokens as counted by the pinned checkpoint's tokenizer. Must not exceed the model's max_len - head_max_len.

tokenizer.description: How the limit is checked BEFORE the request is sent. `pinned_checkpoint`: count with the tokenizer files of the pinned Laya revision. `utf8_byte_upper_bound`: treat the UTF-8 byte length as the token count, a conservative bound for a hosted model whose tokenizer is not available client-side (Jev).

truncation.description: Silent truncation is never allowed; the runtime's own truncation must be disabled or detected.

over_limit.description: An input over token_limit seals ERROR `input_over_context_limit`. ERROR (not INCONCLUSIVE) because the rubric could not be executed as frozen; either way it can never become PASS.

control.description: Known-answer control executed with the same rubric in the same session before the claim. A control that does not map to its expected status makes the claim INCONCLUSIVE `control_failed`. Guards against label-following (for example the documented noul bias on the English checkpoint) and against a silently changed serving stack.

replay.description: Determinism check. Every run maps independently through `decision`; the claim status is the common status only when every run has the identical hard answer, the identical status, and pairwise probability deltas <= probability_epsilon. Any divergence is INCONCLUSIVE with a typed replay reason.

probability_epsilon.description: Maximum absolute difference in the thresholded probability between any two runs. Exists for GPU kernel nondeterminism; pinned CPU fp32 Laya should use a value at or near 1e-6.

freshness.description: At least one run must bypass the AI Gateway cache (`cf-aig-skip-cache`), and/or run on a freshly started model process. A replay set where every run was a cache hit proves nothing about the model and is INCONCLUSIVE `replay_freshness_unmet`.

gateway.description: Serving path. Both backends are reached through the `jev-gateway` Cloudflare Worker, which forwards every call through Cloudflare AI Gateway (Jev as the upstream provider; laya-serve as a custom provider). Only env-var NAMES appear here.

route.description: Jev-compatible decision route (laya-serve exposes the same request/response shape).

mode.description: `enabled_with_bypass_run`: cache is on, but the replay's freshness run sets the skip-cache header. `bypass_all`: no run is served from cache.

key_binds.description: Values folded into the gateway cache key (for example via `cf-aig-cache-key`) so a cached answer can never be served for a different model revision, rubric, or input.

logging.description: AI Gateway logging stays on so every run has a request id and log id recorded in the evidence.

statement.description: The fixed claim, written by the Planning Test Engineer. Never produced or reworded by a backend.

eligibility.description: `closed_option_conformance`: does this fixed input satisfy this fixed, written rule (yes/no or pass/fail options). `closed_option_classification`: which of these fixed categories does the input fall in, where some categories mean holds and others fails.

spec_refs.description: Requirement, design, or published-standard references the rule text derives from.

assurance_eligible.description: True when this rubric may back an `assurance` request. Assurance-eligible rubrics must pin the checkpoint, replay at least twice with a freshness run, and use calibrated probabilities.

question_digest.description: SHA-256 over canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace; the bridge's canonicalJson) of `question`. A served question whose digest differs is ERROR `question_digest_mismatch`.

calibration.description: Laya checkpoints ship over-confident; a frozen temperature fitted on the rubric's calibration set is required.

input.description: Jev's tokenizer is not available client-side, so the limit is enforced on UTF-8 bytes before sending.

path.description: Repository-relative path of a file the validator loads. Never absolute, never `..`.

validator_pin.description: The deterministic program that decides the rule. The runner refuses to run (ERROR `validator_digest_mismatch`) unless every pinned file hashes to its SHA-256 and the module reports this validator_id and version.

implementation.description: The validator module (entry point). SHA-256 over its source bytes.

support_files.description: Every other file the module loads (shared helpers, parsers), each by SHA-256.

runtime_dependencies.description: Node built-ins only; no package is installed or loaded.

validator_rule.description: The rule the program decides, in words, and its condition list in evaluation order (equal to the module's CONDITIONS).

verdict_map.description: Fixed: every condition holds is VERIFIED; any condition fails is REFUTED; input that cannot be read, parsed, or canonicalized is ERROR with a typed reason. A validator has no INCONCLUSIVE outcome of its own (only the runner's control and replay checks produce one).

validator_input_policy.description: What the program reads. The claim's input_digest is SHA-256 over the raw target file bytes; the evidence also records the digest of the canonical form the rule was decided on.

format_by_extension.description: Input format chosen from the target's file extension, never sniffed. An unlisted extension is ERROR `input_unresolvable`.

canonicalization.description: Canonical form the rule is decided on and digested as `canonical_input_digest`.

validator_replay.description: Determinism check with no epsilon: every run decides the input in a freshly started process, and the SHA-256 of every run's canonical decision record must be byte-identical, else INCONCLUSIVE `replay_output_divergence`.

validator_rubric.description: Frozen rubric for the `validator` backend: a deterministic program, not a model. It carries no model, question, thresholds, calibration, temperature, ECE, epsilon, or gateway: same input bytes, same verdict. Replay requires byte-identical output digests.

eligibility.description: The rule is expressible as code and is decided exactly by the pinned program.

assurance_eligible.description: True only when the program agrees with an independent labeler on 100% of the rule's labeled dataset and every control lands on its expected verdict.

rubric.description: (a) Frozen rubric. Pins exactly one backend; discriminated on `backend`. The rubric's own digest (SHA-256 over canonical JSON of the whole rubric document) is its identity inside claims and evidence; any edit is a new rubric_version and a plan amendment.

claim_binding.description: The planVerification `claim` object for a system1 request. Its canonical JSON is stored as `command_configuration.claim`. It binds the frozen rubric by id, version, and digest, and the exact canonicalized input by digest; it carries no free text a backend could reinterpret.

command_configuration.description: (b) Exactly the object planVerification builds and stores in both request and receipt (they must be deeply equal). `claim` is canonical JSON (sorted keys) of a `claim_binding`. `args` is empty: every run parameter (thresholds, replay, cache policy, checkpoint) is pinned by the rubric digest, so command-line overrides are not permitted.

target.description: Repository-relative locator of the input under test, resolved per the rubric's input.source.

executable.description: The caller's verdict-only runner (for example a small client that posts to jev-gateway). Never a generation CLI.

answer.description: Hard answer: the argmax option key (choice), level index as a decimal string (score), or `yes`/`no` (noul).

option_probabilities.description: Calibrated probability per option as used for mapping (noul: {"yes": p, "no": 1-p}).

raw_probabilities.description: Uncalibrated probabilities as served, kept for audit.

thresholded_probability.description: Calibrated mass of the option set containing `answer` (holds or fails set); 0 when the answer is in neither.

served_model_revision.description: Revision the server reported (Laya commit sha or Jev model version).

served_checkpoint.description: Laya only: checkpoint named in the served routing metadata.

strength.description: `observed` when every run's answer and probability were read from live responses. `DERIVED ...` when any verdict was recovered (for example reconstructed from an AI Gateway log after a client timeout); sealVerification then seals INCONCLUSIVE with evidence_tier `derived`.

system1_result.description: The single claim result. sealVerification reads `verdict` as the status. `detail` must never contain the phrase `malformed claim` unless the claim binding itself could not be parsed (that is a typed rejection, not a receipt).

reason.description: Typed reason; required for INCONCLUSIVE and ERROR, absent for VERIFIED and REFUTED.

validator_evidence.description: Evidence of one validator run: the pins actually hashed, the input digests, every control's observed verdict, every fresh-process run's decision-record digest, and the decision with its condition list. No probability exists.

validator_result.description: The single claim result of a validator run. sealVerification reads `verdict` as the status. A claim binding the runner cannot parse is ERROR `claim_malformed` whose detail carries the bridge's `malformed claim` marker, so sealVerification rejects it with no receipt; only that result may omit `evidence`.

backend_output.description: (c) What the caller's runner returns and hands to sealVerification. `backend_version` is read from the run and names backend, runtime, and model revision (for example `laya 0.3.20 convaiinnovations/laya@<sha> laya-typed-decisions`, `jev 1.13.0`, or `validator gtm-purchase-event@1.0.0 node22`). `results` holds exactly one claim result. The whole object is digested (SHA-256, canonical JSON) into the receipt `evidence_digest`, so every gateway id and replay value is bound.
